summary: Cambodian authorities repatriated 635 Thai nationals through the Poipet-Aranyaprathet border crossing following a raid on a 13-story building housing scam operations. Thai police identified 68 individuals with online complaints and two with active arrest warrants. Officials estimate nearly 10,000 Thais remain involved in such operations across the border.
title: Cambodia pushes back 635 Thais after Poipet scam raid

summary: The Thai government is preparing to officially notify Cambodia of its intent to cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims. The proposal is set to be presented to the Cabinet on May 5, 2026. This move comes as Thailand seeks a more modern legal framework for negotiations, though it has sparked warnings from Cambodia regarding regional stability.
title: Thai government to inform Cambodia of intent to scrap 2001 Maritime MoU

summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow revealed that the Philippines has offered to facilitate dialogue between Thailand and Cambodia to ease ongoing tensions. A trilateral meeting may take place during the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu from May 6-8. Thailand is seeking a new negotiation framework based on international maritime law (UNCLOS) and emphasizes the need for a 'ceasefire in statements' to rebuild trust.
title: Manila offers to mediate Thai-Cambodia talks

summary: A popular social media page focusing on border maps raised concerns regarding the construction of a fence along the Thai-Cambodian border near Sisaket. The report claims the Thai military is strictly monitoring the area but keeping the project quiet to avoid Cambodian pressure, despite border markers 52-54 supposedly being settled.
title: Famous page asks why Thailand is hesitant to announce border fence construction

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs is preparing to revoke the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) with Cambodia. Officials intend to shift toward the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to resolve the long-standing 26,000-square-kilometer Overlapping Claims Area (OCA) in the Gulf of Thailand. This strategic move follows Cambodia's recent accession to UNCLOS in February 2026.
title: Thailand eyes UN maritime law to resolve Cambodia border dispute

summary: The Thai government is strengthening cooperation with the US to dismantle major call center networks and human trafficking rings operating along the Thai-Cambodian border. Recent operations discovered over 10,000 victims of forced labor and romance scams of various nationalities. The Prime Minister emphasized that Thailand will not be a transit point for these criminal organizations and aims to reach Tier 1 status in the TIP report.
title: Thailand-US Expand Cooperation to Combat Scammers and Human Trafficking Near Borders

summary: Cambodian authorities released 635 Thai nationals through the Ban Khlong Luek border checkpoint in Sa Kaeo after a major crackdown on online scam networks. The handover was coordinated by multiple agencies, including the Burapha Task Force. Officials are screening returnees to distinguish between victims of forced labor and those knowingly involved in criminal activity; at least one individual was found to have an active arrest warrant.
title: Cambodia scam crackdown sends 635 Thais back home

summary: Cambodian analysts and officials have reacted strongly to statements made by Thailand's UN representative regarding historical aid provided to Cambodia. While Thailand claims its past support justifies current border security measures, Cambodian experts call this a distortion of history. They allege that Thai blockades have displaced thousands of Cambodian households and claim that Thailand is using the narrative of 'gratitude' to mask violations of sovereignty. Tensions remain high as both sides exchange accusations of initiating armed attacks last year.
title: Experts reject Thai claims of past aid to justify actions against Cambodia

source: Daily News (เดลินิวส์)
summary: The Burapha Task Force, in coordination with Aranyaprathet immigration and customs, processed the repatriation of 55 Cambodian nationals (34 men, 19 women, and 2 children) at the Ban Khlong Luek Permanent Border Checkpoint in Sa Kaeo. These individuals had completed their legal sentences for various offenses. Thai authorities handed them over to Cambodian officials at the Thai-Cambodian Friendship Bridge. Security remains tight along the border to maintain stability according to army policy.
title: Thai Burapha Task Force Pushes 55 Cambodians Back Across Border After Legal Cases End

summary: Reporting on the statements from Cambodian officials, Thai media highlights the growing friction over the maritime dispute. Kung Phoak stated that the MoU 44 was intended to resolve overlapping claims through joint development while respecting sovereignty, but lamented that the mechanism has barely been utilized. With Thailand moving toward cancellation, the focus shifts to UNCLOS as the new arena for mediation. This follows earlier positions from Thai officials who suggested a similar shift toward international standards if bilateral talks fail.
title: Cambodian Minister Disappointed as Thailand Set to Cancel MOU 44; Both Nations to Deal via UNCLOS

summary: Phnom Penh has warned it will invoke the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) for 'compulsory conciliation' if Thailand unilaterally withdraws from the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding. Cambodia argues the MoU has been the primary framework for 25 years and its removal would dismantle the only platform for direct bilateral negotiations.
title: Cambodia signals UNCLOS route if Thailand scraps maritime MoU

summary: Following two rounds of armed conflict last year that killed nearly 150 people, the Thai government has formally cancelled MOU 44. PM Anutin, who campaigned on a nationalist platform, stated that the 2001 pact failed to yield results. In response, Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn expressed regret and announced that Cambodia will initiate a compulsory conciliation mechanism under UNCLOS. Although a ceasefire has been in place since late December 2025, Thai officials confirmed that border checkpoints will remain closed until Cambodia fully complies with the joint ceasefire terms.
title: Thailand scraps sea boundary pact with Cambodia

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced that the Thai Cabinet has officially resolved to cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia. He stated the cancellation is due to a lack of progress over 25 years and emphasized it is not related to existing border conflicts. The Thai government will now refer to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) for future negotiations. Anutin assured that security forces are maintaining strict vigilance along the border, but the situation remains stable.
title: PM Anutin says Cabinet axes MOU 44, confident it won't impact border

summary: In response to Thailand's unilateral cancellation of the 2001 MOU, Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn announced that Cambodia will initiate 'compulsory conciliation' under UNCLOS. Cambodia expressed deep regret over the decision, stating that the MOU was the only bilateral framework for peaceful boundary delimitation. While the conciliation outcome is non-binding, it signals Cambodia's move to take the dispute to an international level.
title: Maritime row deepens — Cambodia seeks UNCLOS conciliation after Thai rejection

summary: Government spokesperson Ratchada Thanadirek clarified that the Cabinet's decision to scrap the maritime agreement is a strategic move to 'upgrade negotiation tools' rather than a severance of ties. The government intends to use the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to ensure a more systematic and international approach to the dispute. Thailand has informally notified Cambodia and is preparing a formal letter to follow.
title: Government Emphasizes Cancelling 1994 MOU Is Not Ending Negotiations, Uses UNCLOS Framework to Enhance National Interest Protection

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced that the Thai Cabinet has officially voted to terminate the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia. Anutin argued that the 25-year-old agreement has seen no progress and that Thailand will shift to using the UNCLOS framework instead. He reassured the public that the military remains on high alert and that the cancellation should not increase border tensions, noting that security forces report a stabilizing situation.
title: PM Anutin reveals Cabinet resolution to cancel MOU 44, confident it won't affect border

summary: Government spokesperson Ratchada Thanadirek clarified that revoking MOU 44 is a 'realignment' of the framework rather than a cut in relations. Thailand plans to use the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to resolve maritime disputes more systematically. The government is preparing to formally notify Cambodia and will establish new technical and legal committees to handle the transition under the new international law framework.
title: Government shifts to international law for maritime dispute after ending MOU 44

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the Cabinet's move to scrap the 2001 maritime MoU is a fulfillment of his election campaign promise and is not linked to any specific border clashes. He assured the public that the termination would not escalate tensions at the border. Thai officials will now use UNCLOS as the primary reference for future negotiations.
title: Cabinet cancels MOU 44, Anutin confident border situation won't be affected

summary: Cambodia expressed deep regret after the Thai Cabinet voted to terminate the 2001 maritime agreement. Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn stated that Cambodia now has 'no option' but to initiate compulsory conciliation under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Despite the termination, Cambodia maintains that its lawful rights over maritime areas remain unaffected.
title: Cambodia disappointed as Thailand unilaterally cancels MOU 44, insists on using UNCLOS for maritime dispute

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced that the Thai Cabinet has officially approved the cancellation of the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia. He emphasized that Thailand will shift to using the UNCLOS framework for future negotiations and assured the public that the decision would not negatively impact border security, which remains under military watch.
title: Thai PM says MOU 44 no longer exists after Cabinet approval to cancel maritime deal

summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Cambodian PM Hun Manet met in Cebu for a trilateral meeting with the Philippine President. Both leaders agreed to have their foreign ministers develop 'practical, confidence-building measures' to normalize relations following the deadly border clashes of late 2025.
title: Thailand-Cambodia: Prime Minister reveals 'happy' 3-way talks, moves forward to restore relations and create peace

summary: Thai media reports on the strategic implications of the meeting in Cebu. Analysis suggests that Thailand's recent move to cancel MOU 44 regarding overlapping maritime areas is a major turning point. The report discusses how Cambodia is using international platforms and ASEAN mediation to pressure Thailand over the Koh Kood territory and maritime borders.
title: Cebu Trap: Decoding Cambodia's plan to surround Thailand on the global stage

summary: Following a trilateral meeting in Cebu between PM Anutin Charnvirakul, Cambodian PM Hun Manet, and Philippine President Marcos Jr, both nations are considering returning charges d'affaires to their embassies. Thailand has officially notified Cambodia of its intent to cancel MoU 44 regarding overlapping maritime claims, moving instead toward negotiations under the UNCLOS framework. Both sides agreed to avoid 'verbal wars' to rebuild trust.
title: Thailand and Cambodia Consider Small Diplomatic Step After Border Tensions

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) clarified a viral report about Cambodian soldiers encroaching on Thai territory in Buriram province. Investigations confirmed they were local Thai citizens who regularly speak Khmer in daily life. No gunshots were fired as rumored. The Army urged the public to verify information before sharing to avoid panic.
title: Army Clarifies: Misunderstanding Over Cambodian Incursion in Buriram; Actually Thai Citizens Speaking Khmer

summary: Thai anti-human trafficking police arrested 4 suspects in a major transnational crime network that lured Thai citizens to Cambodia. The gang reportedly has over 40 members and targets Thais looking for work, transporting them to the border where Cambodian partners pick them up.
title: Human Trafficking Network Busted: Thais Lured to Cambodia for Facial Scanning Scams

summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow dismissed concerns that Cambodia's alleged registration of MoU 44 before Thailand's official cancellation would harm Thailand's sovereignty over Koh Kut island. Meanwhile, a military security source revealed that the Thai military has started building a 1.3-kilometer border fence along the frontier in Pong Nam Ron district of Chanthaburi province to enhance safety.

summary: The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Military and State Security, Somboon Noonnual, stated that the situation along the Thailand-Cambodia border is currently normal and peaceful. He addressed reports of gunfire from the Cambodian side, characterizing it as an attempt by Cambodia to create a narrative and spin nationalist sentiments, emphasizing that the firing took place strictly within Cambodian territory and did not cross into Thailand. He acknowledged that Thailand's recent cancellation of MOU 44 played a role in inducing Cambodia to adhere more strictly to international frameworks, while confirming that the Thai military remains patient and prepared, including plans to construct border fences in appropriate locations.
title: Senate Military Committee Chairman insists Thailand-Cambodia border remains peaceful, dismisses Cambodian gunfire as 'image-making'

summary: The Thai Navy Chief of Staff confirmed that the situation along the eastern border with Cambodia, specifically in Chanthaburi and Trat provinces, remains under control with no provocations reported.
title: Navy Chief of Staff confirms border situation in Trat and Chanthaburi is normal and under control

summary: Admiral Thadawut Thadpithakkul, Chief of Staff of the Royal Thai Navy, stated that the border situation between Thailand and Cambodia adjacent to Trat province remains completely normal. The Chanthaburi and Trat Border Defense Command has full control over the situation, and there have been no provocations from the other side.
title: Navy chief of staff confirms eastern Thailand-Cambodia border normal, 100% under control

summary: Thai security forces, including officers from the Chanthaburi and Trat Border Defence Command, arrested 17 individuals in Pong Nam Ron district of Chanthaburi province for illegal border crossing. The detainees included 13 Cambodian migrant workers without valid travel documents fleeing economic hardship, one Thai driver smuggling them, and two Thai nationals returning from Pailin province, Cambodia. The two Thais admitted to working as administrators for an online gambling operation but fled after Cambodian authorities launched heavy crackdowns on scam networks.
title: 17 illegal border-crossers arrested in Chanthaburi

summary: An ad hoc Senate committee has recommended the revocation of the 2000 MOU on border affairs, citing legal flaws regarding disputed French-era maps and arguing that the existing framework has failed to prevent tensions and address border encroachment.
title: Senate panel urges scrapping of MOU43, citing legal flaws and disputed maps

summary: Thai rangers from the 12th Ranger Control Unit in Sa Kaeo province negotiated with Cambodian military personnel after Cambodian villagers brought tractors to prepare farmland in a disputed border area between markers Jor Tor Sor 42 and 44. Thai authorities presented GPS data showing the activity violated MOU 43 by crossing beyond the agreed red-line boundary into territory Thailand considers under its sovereignty. Following the discussion, Cambodian authorities agreed to have the villagers stop their farming activities until the formal border line is officially clarified.
title: Thai rangers halt Cambodian farming activity in Sa Kaeo border area

summary: The Thai Senate reviewed a study conducted by an extraordinary committee led by Senator Noppadol Inna regarding the pros and cons of cancelling the 2000 and 2001 MOUs (MOU 43 and MOU 44). The committee unanimously proposed that the government revoke MOU 43, following the previous cabinet decision on May 5 to scrap MOU 44, citing constitutional compliance issues and 26 years of stagnant border demarcation. However, minority senators, including Pornchai Wityalertpan, strongly opposed the move, warning that canceling it without strong justification could allow corporate groups to seize overlapping maritime energy interests and leave Thailand at a disadvantage.
title: Senate committee urges government to scrap MOU 43; minority senators fear Thailand could lose advantage to Cambodia

summary: Following a shooting incident on May 13, 2026, where Cambodian soldiers fired 11 shots into Thai territory near Chong O'Smach, Surin province, experts are questioning whether the border situation, which has been quiet for five months, is escalating again.
title: Thai PBS: Border gunfire concerns

summary: Defense Minister Lt. Gen. Adul Boonthamcharoen stated that a small Joint Border Committee (GBC) sub-committee has been sent to discuss border issues with Cambodia before full-scale talks. He emphasized that reopening border checkpoints is the final step, contingent on both sides adhering to the Joint Statement and improving the situation. He noted that both nations are preparing their defenses due to recent past conflicts.
title: Border tension flares? 'Big Dul' sends small GBC team to clear up Cambodian soldiers' movements, confirms both sides must protect sovereignty

summary: Defense Minister Adul Boonthamcharoen stated that Thai-Cambodian GBC secretariats must hold preliminary discussions before the next general meeting. He emphasized that reopening border checkpoints will be the final issue considered, depending on the overall security situation.

Malee Sojiata denied that Cambodian forces fired five shots near Border Marker 18 in Surin province on May 21, calling the Thai army's report 'false information' intended to stir tension. title: Senate committee briefs ASEAN+3 ambassadors on the government's plan to cancel MOU 2543 and 2544

The committee claims the agreements have failed to progress over 26 years and accuses Cambodia of encroaching on disputed areas and attempting to unilaterally claim petroleum resources.

title: Royal Thai Army confirms readiness to handle situation after reports of Cambodia using prisoners at border

The Royal Thai Army stated no injuries occurred and no return fire was initiated, but condemned the incident as a violation of the existing ceasefire agreement.

title: One year of border clashes: 13 conflict points mark the rift between Thailand and Cambodia
